result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cap the text measure, scroll code blocks inside their own container, and replace the right column with an inline disclosure at about 1100px. A uses one shared container for the header and body, so the edges line up and the grid holds together, while B's full-width header doesn't line up with its centered 1320px layout on wide screens. On mobile, A turns the left nav into a disclosure; B stacks the whole nav above the article, which pushes the content down. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers cap the measure, use a minmax(0,1fr) grid with min-width:0 so code scrolls inside its own block, and swap the right column for an inline 'On this page' disclosure around 1100px. B is a bit better on the grid and on mobile: the header shares the shell container so its edges line up with the columns, and on phones the left nav becomes a disclosure rather than a long stacked list above the content. B's width estimate at 1280px is slightly off, because its gap is about 38px from the clamp rather than the stated 48px, but the layout itself still works.
